loss_contingencies.definition: Existing condition involving uncertainty that may result in loss
loss_contingencies.disclosure_only: If reasonably possible (but not probable), disclose in notes - do not accrue
loss_contingencies.no_action: If remote (slight chance), no accrual and no disclosure required (exception: guarantees always disclosed)

probability_levels.remote: <25% likely - NO accrual, NO disclosure (except guarantees)

measurement.range_of_estimates: If one amount in range more likely, use that. If no amount more likely, use MINIMUM amount in range (most conservative).
measurement.example: Lawsuit est. loss $100K-$500K, no amount more likely → Accrue $100K (minimum)

gain_contingencies.accounting: Do NOT accrue gains until realized (conservatism)
gain_contingencies.disclosure: Disclose if probable, but avoid misleading language about likelihood
gain_contingencies.example: Lawsuit in company's favor - do not recognize gain until case settled and cash received

warranties.assurance_warranty: Standard warranty assuring product works → Accrue under ASC 450 as loss contingency
warranties.service_warranty: Extended warranty purchased separately → Performance obligation under ASC 606

commitments.definition: Obligation to perform in future (e.g., purchase commitments, employment contracts)
commitments.accounting: Generally not recorded until performance occurs, but disclose if material
commitments.loss_on_purchase_commitment: If committed to purchase at price > market, accrue loss if probable and estimable

cpa_exam_tips: Gain contingencies: Never accrue, only disclose if probable
Range with no best estimate: Use minimum

key_points: Loss contingencies: Probable + Estimable → Accrue. Reasonably possible → Disclose.
Gain contingencies: Never accrue, disclose if probable
Warranties: Assurance type → Accrue as contingency
Range of estimates: Use minimum if no amount more likely
